newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks rise on year-end buying.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks rise on year-end buying.

text.p: Jordanian shares rose at start of weekly trade on Saturday with an increase in portfolio buying to bolster end-of-year balance sheets, dealers said.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 0.37 percent to 151.72 points in high turnover of 2,769,534 dinars ($3,911,771), mostly dominated by large bloc sales.
Brokers said the main pattern of trade on Saturday was a continuation of last week's portfolio buying to prop up closing prices of stocks in end-of-year "window dressing" transactions.
"Portfolios, especially of the larger institutions particularly banks, were in the market to raise prices for end-of-year closing levels," one broker said.
Heavy weight Arab Bank dominated trade in a large bloc sale of 3,000 stocks worth a total of 919,020 dinars with the stock rising 1 dinars to 250 dinars.
The second largest bloc sale was in the blue-chip industrial firm Jordan Cement Factories which shed 0.03 dinars to 3.37 dinars in a deal valued at 674,505 dinars.
The third heaviest traded stock was also a bloc sale worth a total of 360,000 dinars in Jordan Invesment Finance Bank.
In comparison, two banks, Middle East Investment Bank and Jordan Kuwait Bank, were targets of investor buying with a 0.05 dinar rise to 1.06 dinars and a 0.04 dinar rise to 2.84 dinars respectively.

Insurance company Al-Nisr al-Arabi continued its unpward trend to rise the maximum 5 percent daily ceiling to 5.88 dinars on expectations that the one million dinar capitalised firm could issue a 20 percent cash dividend.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange rose 0.45 percent to 82.76 points from 82.38 points, still 13.35 percent down from the start of the year.
Rising shares outnumbered losers on Saturday by 28 to 13, with shares in nine other firms trading but closing unchanged.
